children: Financial stocks took center stage this week as investors digested a wave of third-quarter earnings from major sector leaders.
The Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund
continues to lag the broader market, posting a 4.57% year-to-date gain against a 7.43% rally for the S&P 500 Index.

Across this week’s earnings roundup, 15 financial companies reported results, delivering a strong beat rate against Wall Street expectations for both top- and bottom-line figures. However, Y/Y results were more mixed, as profit growth generally lagged revenue expansion across the group.
Financial Earnings Roundup
Bottom Line:

Of the 15 financial companies with analyst estimates, 13 beat non-GAAP EPS estimates, one missed and one came in line, resulting in an 86.7% beat rate. On a Y/Y basis, across all 16 companies, nine (56.3%) reported Y/Y EPS growth.
Top Line:
Of the 15 financial companies, 11 beat revenue expectations and four missed, resulting in a 73.3% beat rate. On a Y/Y basis, 13 of the 16 companies (81.3%) reported revenue growth. Loews
, which had no analyst consensus estimates, was excluded from the beat-rate calculation.
Let’s take a look at some financial sector companies that reported earnings this week:
Block

reported non-GAAP EPS of $1.13, beating estimates by $0.10, while revenue rose 10% Y/Y to $6.72B, topping expectations by $120M. Growth was supported by a 22% increase in gross profit to $3.24B, with Square gross profit up 14%. Adjusted operating income surged 92% to $923M. Management raised its 2026 outlook and expects at least 15% gross profit growth in 2027.
Allstate

posted non-GAAP EPS of $9.76, beating estimates by $2.80, while revenue increased 0.6% Y/Y to $17.35B but missed forecasts by $110M. Its Property-Liability combined ratio was 86.6%, with higher catastrophe losses adding 7.1 percentage points. The insurer returned $1.5B to shareholders during the quarter and said it plans to launch sales-related AI capabilities in early 2027.
Prudential Financial

reported non-GAAP EPS of $3.77, beating estimates by $0.45, while revenue declined 16.9% Y/Y to $13.49B, missing forecasts by $672M. AUM remained broadly stable at $1.616T, compared with $1.612T in the prior-year quarter.
Fiserv

delivered non-GAAP EPS of $1.75, beating estimates by $0.04, while revenue fell 1.4% Y/Y to $4.85B but topped expectations. Organic revenue was flat, with Merchant Solutions down 2% and Financial Solutions up 2%.

CEO Takis Georgakopoulos said revenue had stabilized after the second-quarter trough and expected Merchant revenue to return to growth in the fourth quarter. Fiserv also reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.20–$7.40.
American International Group

posted non-GAAP EPS of $2.06, beating estimates by $0.18, while revenue increased 17.2% Y/Y to $7.44B, exceeding expectations by $28.9M. The firm returned $787M to shareholders, including $527M in buybacks, and expected the full-year 2026 General Insurance expense ratio to be approximately 30.5%.
Aflac

reported EPS of $2.43, beating estimates by $0.63, while revenue fell 2.6% Y/Y to $4.30B but topped expectations by $90M. EPS declined 2.4% from a year earlier, indicating that the earnings beat did not translate into Y/Y growth.
MetLife

delivered non-GAAP EPS of $2.78, beating estimates by $0.01, while revenue rose 11.2% Y/Y to $19.91B but missed estimates by $63.7M. Adjusted EPS increased 22% to $2.85, supported in part by $720M in variable investment income. CEO Michel Khalaf called it the company's highest adjusted EPS quarter.
Other Financial Companies
The remaining companies also posted mostly positive results. Assurant
, Franklin Resources
, Corpay
, Fidelity National Information Services
, and Jack Henry & Associates
beat both EPS and revenue estimates.
Meanwhile, Global Payments
met EPS expectations and narrowly beat revenue estimates by approximately $267K, while Apollo Global Management
missed EPS expectations but exceeded revenue forecasts.
Loews
reported EPS of $1.50 and revenue of $4.76B; compared with the prior-year period, EPS fell 38.3% while revenue increased 1.9% Y/Y.
Overall, the sector's results showed stronger revenue growth than earnings growth.
Earnings ahead:
Investors will watch KKR & Co.
, which is scheduled to report its results next week.
